prerequisites: Knowledge of First-Year Mathematics, Calculus and Algebra, as well as First-Year Mechanics Physics and Chemistry.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and Application of applied thermodynamics, first principle, second and third principle.
Application of the first principle for Closed and Open Systems.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

syllabus_topics: APPLICATION OF 1ST AND 2ND PRINCIPLES TO OPEN SYSTEMS. ANALYSIS OF ADIABATIC FLOW
APPLICATION OF 1ST AND 2ND PRINCIPLES TO POWER CYCLES WITH INDUSTRIAL INTEREST
APPLICATION OF 1ST AND 2ND PRINCIPLES TO INVERSE CYCLES WITH INDUSTRIAL INTEREST
EXERGETIC ANALYSIS IN INDUSTRIAL APPLICATION SYSTEMS
teaching_methods: Participative lectures, conferences, company visits, fair attendance.
Individual or group problem-solving, case studies, role-playing, technical application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates.
Laboratory activities in specialized facilities, research sessions on classroom didactics.
Integrated project work for problem-solving or task completion through planning, design, and execution of activities.
Personalized and small group tutoring, scheduled tutorials to review materials, learning, and work completion.
Group work including preparation of essays, problem-solving, and projects for submission and presentation in practical classes.
Individual study including preparation for readings, exams, exercises, and classes.

assessment_methods.method: Reports and results of practical execution tests

assessment_rules: For the first call, evaluation includes three written tests (26.25%, 26.25%, 11.25%), practical execution reports (11.25%), and an Integrated Project (25%). The average of all components before the Integrated Project must be 3.5 out of 10. A minimum final grade of 5 out of 10 is required to pass. If a student does not complete the Integrated Project, they need a minimum of 4 in the first two partials to average. For the second call, students may opt to keep their Integrated Project grade (25%) and take an exam for the remaining 75%, or take an exam covering 100% of the grade. If partials are averaged with the Integrated Project, a minimum of 4 in the partials is required.
